name: Bidyara/Gungabula
catalog_quote: c. Bidyara / Gungabula (Breen 1973) Pama-Nyungan, South Queensland, Australia - Main stress is initial. Secondary stress on odd nonfinal syllables, e.g. 10, 100, 1020, 10200, 102020 - Morphology influences stress. Minimal word is disyllabic; no phonemic vowel length.

audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict, initial main stress + secondary on odd non-final syllables (10 100 1010 10100...)' rests on Hayes 1995:199's digest of Breen 1973, read as Google Books snippets; no file of Hayes or Breen is held, so the verbatim check cannot be done (quote_check = no-held-file). Independent secondaries that all trace to Breen 1973 agree: Gordon 2002 appendix (held, refs/:2945 'Odd numbered from L minus final'), Kager 1995 (fetched sources now, PDF p.6, list 6a: rightward trochees, no final stresses, no length contrast), ST0 note '1L, i2@1L, no 1R'. The one first-hand description we hold, Holmer 1983 PL D-54 (salvage survey), says word stress is not distinctive and that longer words tend to stress the SECOND syllable with alternating secondaries (pp. 6, 178, 204-205) — but Holmer makes this identical claim for every language in the volume, from rememberers, so it is weak evid

sources.quote: '(6) No sub-minimal words, no final stresses (20) a. No length contrast (8): Bidyara/Gungubala (Breen 1973), Diyari (Austin 1981), ...' — i.e. Kager files Bidyara as a left-to-right trochaic system with no final (degenerate-foot) stress and no length contrast, citing Breen 1973.
